## New Jersey Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]
Source: https://bankaccountlevy.com/states/new-jersey.html

← bankaccountlevy.com home

New Jersey Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New Jersey residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in New Jersey

New Jersey is one of the most debtor-friendly states for exempt-funds protection. The wage-exemption floor (90% earnings for low-income; 75% otherwise) substantially exceeds the federal CCPA standard, and SSA/SSDI funds deposited in accounts receive both federal and state protection.

Income SourceNew Jersey Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)90% earnings for low-income; 75% otherwise

Head-of-household boostStrong low-income earner protection

Levy protest deadline10 days (exemption claim)

42 U.S.C. 407 + N.J.S.A. 2A:17-56 state mirror

42 U.S.C. 407 - Federal SSA Protection

Section 407 of Title 42 of the U.S. Code provides absolute protection for Social Security and SSDI benefits: "none of the moneys paid or payable or rights existing under this subchapter shall be subject to execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process." This protection applies in every state, including New Jersey.

The protection applies to:

Social Security retirement benefits

Social Security disability (SSDI)

Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

Survivors' benefits

Auxiliary benefits (for dependents)

The Treasury Department's 2011 rule (31 CFR Part 212) requires banks to automatically protect up to 2 months of federal benefit deposits when a levy arrives. Treasury 2-month rule applies.

State Wage Exemptions in New Jersey

After wages hit your bank account, the separate bank-account exemptions apply. In New Jersey: 90% earnings for low-income; 75% otherwise.

Strong low-income earner protection

Critical practice point: the wage exemption protects earnings "in the hands of the employer," but once they deposit into your checking account they become "funds" rather than "wages." Some states preserve wage-exempt status for a limited period after deposit; others do not. Check your New Jersey rules before assuming deposited wages retain garnishment protection.

Head-of-Household Exemption in New Jersey

Strong low-income earner protection

Where head-of-household status applies, the protection can dwarf the federal CCPA floor. The classic example is Florida: a head of family earning under $750/week is fully exempt from wage garnishment for consumer debt. Missouri caps head-of-family garnishment at 10% rather than 25%. Nebraska's 85% HOH protection is also notable.

To claim HOH status in most states, you must:

Provide more than half the support of a dependent living in your household, and

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Levy-Protest Procedure in New Jersey

Deadline: 10 days (exemption claim). File N.J. Ct. R. 4:59-1 claim; bank releases on court order.

The New Jersey stop-levy checklist:

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

Gather documentation. Deposit slips, pay stubs, SSA award letters, dependent documentation for HOH claim.

File claim-of-exemption. Use the form specified in File N.J. Ct. R. 4:59-1 claim; bank releases on court order. above.

Request hearing. Most courts set a levy-protest hearing within 7-14 days.

Serve the bank. Once the court orders release, serve the order on the levying bank.

The Treasury 2-Month SSA Rule

Treasury 2-month rule applies.

When a bank receives a levy, it must "look back" 2 months at direct-deposit records. If any federal-benefit deposit (Social Security, SSI, VA, federal retirement) arrived during that window, the bank must automatically exempt up to 2 times the monthly deposit amount. This rule is self-executing - the bank does it without a court order.

Common failures:

Benefits paid by paper check rather than direct deposit - not auto-protected.

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

New Jersey Federal Bankruptcy Data

When levy-protection fails administratively, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts the levy within 24 hours. These FJC numbers show how New Jersey debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,580 consumer bankruptcy cases from New Jersey's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 752697.3%2.7%

Chapter 131,05431.0%68.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

How Bankruptcy Stops a New Jersey Levy Immediately

The bankruptcy automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts all levies within 24 hours of filing. For New Jersey debtors facing a bank-account levy:

Chapter 7 filing triggers the stay; typical discharge in 90 days.

Chapter 13 filing same stay; 3-5-year reorganization plan.

Preference clawback under 11 U.S.C. Section 547 may recover levied funds if total exceeds $600 within 90 days before filing.

Exemption claim under 11 U.S.C. Section 522 protects account balance up to New Jersey exemption caps.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, New Jersey means test, and levy prevention strategies.

## New York Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]
Source: https://bankaccountlevy.com/states/new-york.html

New York Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New York residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in New York

New York is one of the most debtor-friendly states for exempt-funds protection. The wage-exemption floor (90% earnings or 30x fed MW (very strong)) substantially exceeds the federal CCPA standard, and SSA/SSDI funds deposited in accounts receive both federal and state protection.

Income SourceNew York Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)90% earnings or 30x fed MW (very strong)

Head-of-household boostNo HOH-specific boost, but strongest SSA-in-bank protection

Levy protest deadline20 days (EIPA claim)

42 U.S.C. 407 + CPLR 5222-a (Exempt Income Protection Act)

42 U.S.C. 407 - Federal SSA Protection

Section 407 of Title 42 of the U.S. Code provides absolute protection for Social Security and SSDI benefits: "none of the moneys paid or payable or rights existing under this subchapter shall be subject to execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process." This protection applies in every state, including New York.

Social Security disability (SSDI)

Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

Survivors' benefits

Auxiliary benefits (for dependents)

The Treasury Department's 2011 rule (31 CFR Part 212) requires banks to automatically protect up to 2 months of federal benefit deposits when a levy arrives. Treasury 2-month rule + NY's EIPA provides among strongest SSA-in-bank protection in US.

State Wage Exemptions in New York

After wages hit your bank account, the separate bank-account exemptions apply. In New York: 90% earnings or 30x fed MW (very strong).

No HOH-specific boost, but strongest SSA-in-bank protection

Critical practice point: the wage exemption protects earnings "in the hands of the employer," but once they deposit into your checking account they become "funds" rather than "wages." Some states preserve wage-exempt status for a limited period after deposit; others do not. Check your New York rules before assuming deposited wages retain garnishment protection.

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Deadline: 20 days (EIPA claim). File CPLR 5222-a claim; bank must unfreeze SSA funds + penalty for wrongful freeze.

The New York stop-levy checklist:

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

Gather documentation. Deposit slips, pay stubs, SSA award letters, dependent documentation for HOH claim.

File claim-of-exemption. Use the form specified in File CPLR 5222-a claim; bank must unfreeze SSA funds + penalty for wrongful freeze. above.

Request hearing. Most courts set a levy-protest hearing within 7-14 days.

Serve the bank. Once the court orders release, serve the order on the levying bank.

The Treasury 2-Month SSA Rule

Treasury 2-month rule + NY's EIPA provides among strongest SSA-in-bank protection in US.

When a bank receives a levy, it must "look back" 2 months at direct-deposit records. If any federal-benefit deposit (Social Security, SSI, VA, federal retirement) arrived during that window, the bank must automatically exempt up to 2 times the monthly deposit amount. Benefits paid by paper check rather than direct deposit - not auto-protected.

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

North Carolina Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for North Carolina residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in North Carolina

North Carolina is one of four states (with Pennsylvania, North Carolina, and South Carolina) that ban wage garnishment for most consumer debts. Bank account levies are still possible, but once funds leave your paycheck and deposit into your account, the protections narrow. Exempt-funds claims and the Treasury 2-month SSA rule become the main protections.

Income SourceNorth Carolina Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)Full wage garnishment ban on consumer debts (NCGS 1-362)

Head-of-household boostN/A - NC bans consumer wage garnishment

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

How Bankruptcy Stops a North Dakota Levy Immediately

The bankruptcy automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts all levies within 24 hours of filing. For North Dakota debtors facing a bank-account levy:

Chapter 7 filing triggers the stay; typical discharge in 90 days.

Chapter 13 filing same stay; 3-5-year reorganization plan.

Preference clawback under 11 U.S.C. Section 547 may recover levied funds if total exceeds $600 within 90 days before filing.

Exemption claim under 11 U.S.C. Section 522 protects account balance up to North Dakota exemption caps.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, North Dakota means test, and levy prevention strategies.

## Ohio Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]
Source: https://bankaccountlevy.com/states/ohio.html

← bankaccountlevy.com home

Ohio Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Ohio residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in Ohio

Ohio tracks the federal CCPA for wage exemptions (75% earnings (follows federal)). Federal 42 U.S.C. 407 fully protects Social Security and SSDI funds; the Treasury 2-month rule auto-protects two months of SSA deposits from any levy.

Income SourceOhio Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)75% earnings (follows federal)

Head-of-household boostHOH boost via homestead

Levy protest deadline5 days (very fast exemption)

42 U.S.C. 407 + ORC 2329.66 state mirror

42 U.S.C. 407 - Federal SSA Protection

Section 407 of Title 42 of the U.S. Code provides absolute protection for Social Security and SSDI benefits: "none of the moneys paid or payable or rights existing under this subchapter shall be subject to execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process." This protection applies in every state, including Ohio.

The protection applies to:

Social Security retirement benefits

Social Security disability (SSDI)

Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

Survivors' benefits

Auxiliary benefits (for dependents)

The Treasury Department's 2011 rule (31 CFR Part 212) requires banks to automatically protect up to 2 months of federal benefit deposits when a levy arrives. Treasury 2-month rule applies.

State Wage Exemptions in Ohio

After wages hit your bank account, the separate bank-account exemptions apply. In Ohio: 75% earnings (follows federal).

HOH boost via homestead

Critical practice point: the wage exemption protects earnings "in the hands of the employer," but once they deposit into your checking account they become "funds" rather than "wages." Some states preserve wage-exempt status for a limited period after deposit; others do not. Check your Ohio rules before assuming deposited wages retain garnishment protection.

Head-of-Household Exemption in Ohio

HOH boost via homestead

Where head-of-household status applies, the protection can dwarf the federal CCPA floor. The classic example is Florida: a head of family earning under $750/week is fully exempt from wage garnishment for consumer debt. Missouri caps head-of-family garnishment at 10% rather than 25%. Nebraska's 85% HOH protection is also notable.

To claim HOH status in most states, you must:

Provide more than half the support of a dependent living in your household, and

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Levy-Protest Procedure in Ohio

Deadline: 5 days (very fast exemption). File ORC 2329.66 hearing request; bank releases on order.

The Ohio stop-levy checklist:

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

Gather documentation. Deposit slips, pay stubs, SSA award letters, dependent documentation for HOH claim.

File claim-of-exemption. Use the form specified in File ORC 2329.66 hearing request; bank releases on order. above.

Request hearing. Most courts set a levy-protest hearing within 7-14 days.

Serve the bank. Once the court orders release, serve the order on the levying bank.

The Treasury 2-Month SSA Rule

Treasury 2-month rule applies.

When a bank receives a levy, it must "look back" 2 months at direct-deposit records. If any federal-benefit deposit (Social Security, SSI, VA, federal retirement) arrived during that window, the bank must automatically exempt up to 2 times the monthly deposit amount. This rule is self-executing - the bank does it without a court order.

Common failures:

Benefits paid by paper check rather than direct deposit - not auto-protected.

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

Ohio Federal Bankruptcy Data

When levy-protection fails administratively, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts the levy within 24 hours. These FJC numbers show how Ohio debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 3,971 consumer bankruptcy cases from Ohio's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 73,53597.7%1.8%

Chapter 1343651.1%48.9%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

How Bankruptcy Stops a Ohio Levy Immediately

The bankruptcy automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts all levies within 24 hours of filing. For Ohio debtors facing a bank-account levy:

Chapter 7 filing triggers the stay; typical discharge in 90 days.

Chapter 13 filing same stay; 3-5-year reorganization plan.

Preference clawback under 11 U.S.C. Section 547 may recover levied funds if total exceeds $600 within 90 days before filing.

Exemption claim under 11 U.S.C. Section 522 protects account balance up to Ohio exemption caps.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Ohio means test, and levy prevention strategies.

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Pennsylvania residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in Pennsylvania

Pennsylvania is one of four states (with Pennsylvania, North Carolina, and South Carolina) that ban wage garnishment for most consumer debts. Bank account levies are still possible, but once funds leave your paycheck and deposit into your account, the protections narrow. Exempt-funds claims and the Treasury 2-month SSA rule become the main protections.

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

## South Carolina Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]
Source: https://bankaccountlevy.com/states/south-carolina.html

← bankaccountlevy.com home

South Carolina Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for South Carolina residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in South Carolina

South Carolina is one of four states (with Pennsylvania, North Carolina, and South Carolina) that ban wage garnishment for most consumer debts. Bank account levies are still possible, but once funds leave your paycheck and deposit into your account, the protections narrow. Exempt-funds claims and the Treasury 2-month SSA rule become the main protections.

Income SourceSouth Carolina Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)Full wage garnishment ban on consumer debts (SC Code 15-39-40)

Head-of-household boostN/A - SC bans consumer wage garnishment

Levy protest deadline10 days (exemption claim)

42 U.S.C. 407 + SC Code 15-41-30 state mirror

42 U.S.C. 407 - Federal SSA Protection

Section 407 of Title 42 of the U.S. Code provides absolute protection for Social Security and SSDI benefits: "none of the moneys paid or payable or rights existing under this subchapter shall be subject to execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process." This protection applies in every state, including South Carolina.

The protection applies to:

Social Security retirement benefits

Social Security disability (SSDI)

Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

Survivors' benefits

Auxiliary benefits (for dependents)

The Treasury Department's 2011 rule (31 CFR Part 212) requires banks to automatically protect up to 2 months of federal benefit deposits when a levy arrives. Treasury 2-month rule applies.

State Wage Exemptions in South Carolina

After wages hit your bank account, the separate bank-account exemptions apply. In South Carolina: Full wage garnishment ban on consumer debts (SC Code 15-39-40).

N/A - SC bans consumer wage garnishment

Critical practice point: the wage exemption protects earnings "in the hands of the employer," but once they deposit into your checking account they become "funds" rather than "wages." Some states preserve wage-exempt status for a limited period after deposit; others do not. Check your South Carolina rules before assuming deposited wages retain garnishment protection.

Head-of-Household Exemption in South Carolina

N/A - SC bans consumer wage garnishment

Where head-of-household status applies, the protection can dwarf the federal CCPA floor. The classic example is Florida: a head of family earning under $750/week is fully exempt from wage garnishment for consumer debt. Missouri caps head-of-family garnishment at 10% rather than 25%. Nebraska's 85% HOH protection is also notable.

To claim HOH status in most states, you must:

Provide more than half the support of a dependent living in your household, and

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Levy-Protest Procedure in South Carolina

Deadline: 10 days (exemption claim). File SC exemption claim; bank releases on court order.

The South Carolina stop-levy checklist:

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

Gather documentation. Deposit slips, pay stubs, SSA award letters, dependent documentation for HOH claim.

File claim-of-exemption. Use the form specified in File SC exemption claim; bank releases on court order. above.

Request hearing. Most courts set a levy-protest hearing within 7-14 days.

Serve the bank. Once the court orders release, serve the order on the levying bank.

The Treasury 2-Month SSA Rule

Treasury 2-month rule applies.

When a bank receives a levy, it must "look back" 2 months at direct-deposit records. If any federal-benefit deposit (Social Security, SSI, VA, federal retirement) arrived during that window, the bank must automatically exempt up to 2 times the monthly deposit amount. This rule is self-executing - the bank does it without a court order.

Common failures:

Benefits paid by paper check rather than direct deposit - not auto-protected.

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

South Carolina Federal Bankruptcy Data

When levy-protection fails administratively, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts the levy within 24 hours. These FJC numbers show how South Carolina debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 635 consumer bankruptcy cases from South Carolina's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7301n/an/a

Chapter 13334n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

How Bankruptcy Stops a South Carolina Levy Immediately

The bankruptcy automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts all levies within 24 hours of filing. For South Carolina debtors facing a bank-account levy:

Chapter 7 filing triggers the stay; typical discharge in 90 days.

Chapter 13 filing same stay; 3-5-year reorganization plan.

Preference clawback under 11 U.S.C. Section 547 may recover levied funds if total exceeds $600 within 90 days before filing.

Exemption claim under 11 U.S.C. Section 522 protects account balance up to South Carolina exemption caps.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, South Carolina means test, and levy prevention strategies.

## Vermont Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]
Source: https://bankaccountlevy.com/states/vermont.html

← bankaccountlevy.com home

Vermont Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Vermont residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in Vermont

Vermont tracks the federal CCPA for wage exemptions (75% earnings + low-earner protection). Federal 42 U.S.C. 407 fully protects Social Security and SSDI funds; the Treasury 2-month rule auto-protects two months of SSA deposits from any levy.

Income SourceVermont Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)75% earnings + low-earner protection

Head-of-household boostNo HOH-specific levy boost

Levy protest deadline20 days (exemption claim)

42 U.S.C. 407 + 12 V.S.A. 2740 state mirror

42 U.S.C. 407 - Federal SSA Protection

Section 407 of Title 42 of the U.S. Code provides absolute protection for Social Security and SSDI benefits: "none of the moneys paid or payable or rights existing under this subchapter shall be subject to execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process." This protection applies in every state, including Vermont.

The protection applies to:

Social Security retirement benefits

Social Security disability (SSDI)

Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

Survivors' benefits

Auxiliary benefits (for dependents)

The Treasury Department's 2011 rule (31 CFR Part 212) requires banks to automatically protect up to 2 months of federal benefit deposits when a levy arrives. Treasury 2-month rule applies.

State Wage Exemptions in Vermont

After wages hit your bank account, the separate bank-account exemptions apply. In Vermont: 75% earnings + low-earner protection.

No HOH-specific levy boost

Critical practice point: the wage exemption protects earnings "in the hands of the employer," but once they deposit into your checking account they become "funds" rather than "wages." Some states preserve wage-exempt status for a limited period after deposit; others do not. Check your Vermont rules before assuming deposited wages retain garnishment protection.

Head-of-Household Exemption in Vermont

No HOH-specific levy boost

Where head-of-household status applies, the protection can dwarf the federal CCPA floor. The classic example is Florida: a head of family earning under $750/week is fully exempt from wage garnishment for consumer debt. Missouri caps head-of-family garnishment at 10% rather than 25%. Nebraska's 85% HOH protection is also notable.

To claim HOH status in most states, you must:

Provide more than half the support of a dependent living in your household, and

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Levy-Protest Procedure in Vermont

Deadline: 20 days (exemption claim). File 12 V.S.A. 3023 claim; bank releases on court order.

The Vermont stop-levy checklist:

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

Gather documentation. Deposit slips, pay stubs, SSA award letters, dependent documentation for HOH claim.

File claim-of-exemption. Use the form specified in File 12 V.S.A. 3023 claim; bank releases on court order. above.

Request hearing. Most courts set a levy-protest hearing within 7-14 days.

Serve the bank. Once the court orders release, serve the order on the levying bank.

The Treasury 2-Month SSA Rule

Treasury 2-month rule applies.

When a bank receives a levy, it must "look back" 2 months at direct-deposit records. If any federal-benefit deposit (Social Security, SSI, VA, federal retirement) arrived during that window, the bank must automatically exempt up to 2 times the monthly deposit amount. This rule is self-executing - the bank does it without a court order.

Common failures:

Benefits paid by paper check rather than direct deposit - not auto-protected.

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

How Bankruptcy Stops a Vermont Levy Immediately

The bankruptcy automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts all levies within 24 hours of filing. For Vermont debtors facing a bank-account levy:

Chapter 7 filing triggers the stay; typical discharge in 90 days.

Chapter 13 filing same stay; 3-5-year reorganization plan.

Preference clawback under 11 U.S.C. Section 547 may recover levied funds if total exceeds $600 within 90 days before filing.

Exemption claim under 11 U.S.C. Section 522 protects account balance up to Vermont exemption caps.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Vermont means test, and levy prevention strategies.

## Virginia Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]
Source: https://bankaccountlevy.com/states/virginia.html

← bankaccountlevy.com home

Virginia Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Virginia residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in Virginia

Virginia tracks the federal CCPA for wage exemptions (75% earnings or 40x fed MW, whichever more). Federal 42 U.S.C. 407 fully protects Social Security and SSDI funds; the Treasury 2-month rule auto-protects two months of SSA deposits from any levy.

Income SourceVirginia Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)75% earnings or 40x fed MW, whichever more

Head-of-household boostHead-of-household $25,000 boost

Levy protest deadline21 days (exemption claim)

42 U.S.C. 407 + Va. Code 34-4 state mirror

42 U.S.C. 407 - Federal SSA Protection

Section 407 of Title 42 of the U.S. Code provides absolute protection for Social Security and SSDI benefits: "none of the moneys paid or payable or rights existing under this subchapter shall be subject to execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process." This protection applies in every state, including Virginia.

The protection applies to:

Social Security retirement benefits

Social Security disability (SSDI)

Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

Survivors' benefits

Auxiliary benefits (for dependents)

The Treasury Department's 2011 rule (31 CFR Part 212) requires banks to automatically protect up to 2 months of federal benefit deposits when a levy arrives. Treasury 2-month rule applies.

State Wage Exemptions in Virginia

After wages hit your bank account, the separate bank-account exemptions apply. In Virginia: 75% earnings or 40x fed MW, whichever more.

Head-of-household $25,000 boost

Critical practice point: the wage exemption protects earnings "in the hands of the employer," but once they deposit into your checking account they become "funds" rather than "wages." Some states preserve wage-exempt status for a limited period after deposit; others do not. Check your Virginia rules before assuming deposited wages retain garnishment protection.

Head-of-Household Exemption in Virginia

Head-of-household $25,000 boost

Where head-of-household status applies, the protection can dwarf the federal CCPA floor. The classic example is Florida: a head of family earning under $750/week is fully exempt from wage garnishment for consumer debt. Missouri caps head-of-family garnishment at 10% rather than 25%. Nebraska's 85% HOH protection is also notable.

To claim HOH status in most states, you must:

Provide more than half the support of a dependent living in your household, and

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Levy-Protest Procedure in Virginia

Deadline: 21 days (exemption claim). File Va. Code 34-17 homestead deed; bank releases on court order.

The Virginia stop-levy checklist:

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

Gather documentation. Deposit slips, pay stubs, SSA award letters, dependent documentation for HOH claim.

File claim-of-exemption. Use the form specified in File Va. Code 34-17 homestead deed; bank releases on court order. above.

Request hearing. Most courts set a levy-protest hearing within 7-14 days.

Serve the bank. Once the court orders release, serve the order on the levying bank.

The Treasury 2-Month SSA Rule

Treasury 2-month rule applies.

When a bank receives a levy, it must "look back" 2 months at direct-deposit records. If any federal-benefit deposit (Social Security, SSI, VA, federal retirement) arrived during that window, the bank must automatically exempt up to 2 times the monthly deposit amount. This rule is self-executing - the bank does it without a court order.

Common failures:

Benefits paid by paper check rather than direct deposit - not auto-protected.

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

Virginia Federal Bankruptcy Data

When levy-protection fails administratively, bankruptcy's automatic stay halts the levy within 24 hours. These FJC numbers show how Virginia debtors use the bankruptcy remedy.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,064 consumer bankruptcy cases from Virginia's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7514n/an/a

Chapter 1355071.2%28.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

How Bankruptcy Stops a Virginia Levy Immediately

The bankruptcy automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts all levies within 24 hours of filing. For Virginia debtors facing a bank-account levy:

Chapter 7 filing triggers the stay; typical discharge in 90 days.

Chapter 13 filing same stay; 3-5-year reorganization plan.

Preference clawback under 11 U.S.C. Section 547 may recover levied funds if total exceeds $600 within 90 days before filing.

Exemption claim under 11 U.S.C. Section 522 protects account balance up to Virginia exemption caps.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Virginia means test, and levy prevention strategies.

## Washington Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]
Source: https://bankaccountlevy.com/states/washington.html

Washington Bank Account Levy: Exempt Funds and Protest Rules [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Washington residents.

Exempt Funds Protection in Washington

Washington tracks the federal CCPA for wage exemptions (75% earnings or 35x state MW, whichever more). Federal 42 U.S.C. 407 fully protects Social Security and SSDI funds; the Treasury 2-month rule auto-protects two months of SSA deposits from any levy.

Income SourceWashington Protection

Social Security / SSDIFully exempt (42 U.S.C. 407)

Wages (state floor)75% earnings or 35x state MW, whichever more

Head-of-household boostHOH protection via homestead

Levy protest deadline14 days (exemption claim)

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Deadline: 14 days (exemption claim). File RCW 6.27 claim; bank releases on court order.

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

42 U.S.C. 407 + Wyo. Stat. 1-20-106 state mirror

42 U.S.C. 407 - Federal SSA Protection

Section 407 of Title 42 of the U.S. Code provides absolute protection for Social Security and SSDI benefits: "none of the moneys paid or payable or rights existing under this subchapter shall be subject to execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process." This protection applies in every state, including Wyoming.

The protection applies to:

Social Security retirement benefits

Social Security disability (SSDI)

Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

Survivors' benefits

Auxiliary benefits (for dependents)

The Treasury Department's 2011 rule (31 CFR Part 212) requires banks to automatically protect up to 2 months of federal benefit deposits when a levy arrives. Treasury 2-month rule applies.

State Wage Exemptions in Wyoming

After wages hit your bank account, the separate bank-account exemptions apply. In Wyoming: 75% earnings (follows federal).

No HOH-specific levy boost

Critical practice point: the wage exemption protects earnings "in the hands of the employer," but once they deposit into your checking account they become "funds" rather than "wages." Some states preserve wage-exempt status for a limited period after deposit; others do not. Check your Wyoming rules before assuming deposited wages retain garnishment protection.

Head-of-Household Exemption in Wyoming

No HOH-specific levy boost

Where head-of-household status applies, the protection can dwarf the federal CCPA floor. The classic example is Florida: a head of family earning under $750/week is fully exempt from wage garnishment for consumer debt. Missouri caps head-of-family garnishment at 10% rather than 25%. Nebraska's 85% HOH protection is also notable.

To claim HOH status in most states, you must:

Provide more than half the support of a dependent living in your household, and

File a sworn affidavit or claim of exemption with the court (timing varies by state).

Levy-Protest Procedure in Wyoming

Deadline: 20 days (exemption claim). File Wyo. Stat. 1-15-511 claim; bank releases on court order.

The Wyoming stop-levy checklist:

Identify the source of funds. SSA/SSDI? Wages? Child support? Tax refund? Each has different protection.

Gather documentation. Deposit slips, pay stubs, SSA award letters, dependent documentation for HOH claim.

File claim-of-exemption. Use the form specified in File Wyo. Stat. 1-15-511 claim; bank releases on court order. above.

Request hearing. Most courts set a levy-protest hearing within 7-14 days.

Serve the bank. Once the court orders release, serve the order on the levying bank.

The Treasury 2-Month SSA Rule

Treasury 2-month rule applies.

When a bank receives a levy, it must "look back" 2 months at direct-deposit records. If any federal-benefit deposit (Social Security, SSI, VA, federal retirement) arrived during that window, the bank must automatically exempt up to 2 times the monthly deposit amount. This rule is self-executing - the bank does it without a court order.

Common failures:

Benefits paid by paper check rather than direct deposit - not auto-protected.

Commingling SSA with other deposits - the 2-month protection is calculated on SSA inflow only.

Account in a third person's name - the rule follows the SSA beneficiary.

If your bank froze an SSA-funded account and did not apply the Treasury rule, file a complaint with the CFPB and demand immediate unfreeze.

How Bankruptcy Stops a Wyoming Levy Immediately

The bankruptcy automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts all levies within 24 hours of filing. For Wyoming debtors facing a bank-account levy:

Chapter 7 filing triggers the stay; typical discharge in 90 days.

Chapter 13 filing same stay; 3-5-year reorganization plan.

Preference clawback under 11 U.S.C. Section 547 may recover levied funds if total exceeds $600 within 90 days before filing.

Exemption claim under 11 U.S.C. Section 522 protects account balance up to Wyoming exemption caps.

See 1328(f) refiling screener, Wyoming means test, and levy prevention strategies.
